_about: Default display duration in minutes per program_type (spec v0.5 P.8). A repo data file, not a table, matching data/render_policies.json. NOTHING READS THIS YET - the renderer and the app pick it up in a later prompt. A program row's expected_duration_min overrides it; open_ended=true means the end is unknown and the card fades right (deferred to rendering contract v1.7).
_provenance: Every entry carries a `source` field. 'render_policies.json' means the number is the sport's existing block_minutes and is AUTHORITATIVE - it is what the grid already draws today. 'provisional' means the Brief 2 research set is the intended authority but has NO REPO COPY (research-nascar.md and its siblings live in the claude.ai project workspace), so the number is a conventional broadcast-window placeholder that has NOT been confirmed against research. Provisional values are safe to use - they are all plausible window lengths - but must be reconciled with research-nascar.md before any of this content ships to a grid.

game.note: Mirrors data/render_policies.json block_minutes exactly, and the fallback matches web/lib/gridmodel.js blockMinutes() (180). If the two ever disagree, render_policies.json wins - it is what the renderer reads.

race_session.note: PENDING research-nascar.md, which is not in this repo - these are conventional broadcast-window lengths, not sourced values. Track type is not yet a column on programs; it arrives with the motorsport adapter. Races default to open_ended because a caution period moves the end time, which is exactly the case P.8 exists for. RACE ONLY - practice and qualifying are out of scope (Joe 2026-09-02).

fight_card.note: One UFC event start to finish - early prelims through main card - which is why it is long. The interior structure is programs.segments, not sibling programs (Joe 2026-09-02). Open-ended because a card's end depends on how many fights go the distance. CBS carries a WINDOW of some events; that is a game_broadcasts row with window_start/window_end, not a shorter program.

weekly_show.note: SmackDown is a 3h show per the Brief 2 rights summary in docs/research/research-changelog.md (2026-09-02 entry: 'SmackDown USA (3h)'); the others are conventional and provisional. NXT is out of scope (Joe 2026-09-02).

special_event.note: WWE PLEs and AEW specials included with a subscription. PPV is EXCLUDED - there is no purchasable access state (Joe 2026-09-02). SNME is modelled here as PLE-class; see spec v0.5 P.11, ASSUMPTION PENDING JOE.

studio_show.note: Pregame/postgame BOOKENDS only - no daily talk or debate shows. A studio show is chipless: it carries the sport it covers so it filters with that sport, but never creates a chip of its own (P.5).
